Hydrogen Economy

Key points covered

  • green and blue hydrogen producers, electrolyzer OEMs, and fuel cell manufacturers
  • Specialist NDT cohorts for hydrogen production, transport, and storage — built around ASME B31.12 hydrogen piping, ASME VIII Div 2 for high-pressure hydrogen vessels, and the additional essential variables required for hydrogen-embrittlement-resistant inspection. Designed for NEOM-scale green hydrogen mega-projects and blue hydrogen with CCS retrofits.
  • Ultrasonic Testing — PAUT for high-pressure hydrogen vessels + TOFD for thick-wall reformers
  • Hydrogen vessel inspectors, electrolyzer stack QC, ammonia carrier inspectors
  • Magnetic Particle Testing — WFMT for hydrogen-embrittlement surface screening
  • Hardness testing + replication for hydrogen-induced cracking surveillance
  • Process-piping QC crews transferred from oil &amp; gas with ASME B31.3 fluency but no B31.12 hydrogen essential-variable training
  • Hydrogen-induced cracking risk under-controlled; commissioning hydro-test failures and EPC schedule slippage measured in months.
  • Pressure-vessel inspectors certified to ASME VIII Div 1 only, encountering hydrogen storage tanks fabricated to Div 2 acceptance criteria
  • Acceptance criteria misapplied; defects accepted that fail Div 2 fitness-for-service, or worse — defects rejected that were acceptable, driving costly rework.
  • PAUT operators trained on hydrocarbon vessels who cannot defend scan plans on hydrogen embrittlement targets (sub-surface micro-cracks, HF-induced cracking)
  • Audit findings during commissioning by hydrogen offtakers (Yara, ADNOC, Aramco, Plug Power) and insurers — scan rejected, vessel re-inspected.
  • Welding inspectors holding generic AWS CWI without hydrogen-specific filler-metal-traceability discipline
  • Heat-affected zone hardness exceedances on hydrogen-service welds; rework cost in the hundreds of thousands per spread on electrolyzer projects.
  • Recurrent training cadence set at SNT-TC-1A's 5-year default rather than the annual recertification typical at hydrogen offtaker audits
  • Insurer surveys and offtaker pre-commissioning audits flag stale qualification records — commercial-operation-date slippage.
  • Level II UT + RT + MT + PT, then API 510 + ASME B31.12 bridging module
  • Level II UT + MT + PT + helium leak, plus stack-specific written practice
  • Level II UT + RT + MT, then API 1104 weld inspection + B31.12 transmission module
  • Multi-asset hydrogen mega-project annual contract; offtaker-specific written-practice bridging included.
  • Hydrogen cohorts are dominated by hybrid delivery. Theory on the LMS during EPC mobilisation, on-site practicals at the electrolyzer OEM stack-test facility or the EPC's hydrogen-service spool fabrication shop two to four weeks before commissioning. PAUT calibration on hydrogen-specific reference blocks (representative of vessel base metal + cladding combinations) is delivered on the customer's own coupons so essential-variable transfer is genuine. Pure on-site delivery is reserved for radiography (regulatory licensing, source storage) and high-pressure helium leak testing.
  • Hydrogen project compliance is governed by a fast-consolidating code stack — ASME B31.12 for piping, ASME VIII Div 2 for vessels, EIGA Doc 100 for industry safety, plus offtaker-specific written practices (NEOM, Yara, Plug Power, Air Liquide, Linde, Nel Hydrogen). We document training records SNT-TC-1A baseline + customer-written-practice overlay + B31.12/Div 2 essential-variable trace through each module. The evidence pack survives both insurer / lender surveys and offtaker commissioning audits without findings.
  • Green hydrogen mega-project (Middle East) — 36-engineer multi-method cohort, 13-week programme
